progressionInfo.name: vi-IV-I-V Progression
progressionInfo.subtitle: The emotional powerhouse of modern pop - starting with melancholy and ending with anticipation, this progression creates a compelling emotional arc.

chordDiagrams.title: Open Position (Key of C)
chordDiagrams.description: The standard open chord voicings for playing vi-IV-I-V in the key of C major.
practiceNotes: Start with clean chord changes before adding rhythm
Focus on the emotional transition from minor to major
Practice smooth voice leading between chords
Experiment with different strumming patterns to enhance the mood

chordDiagrams.title: Seventh Chord Extensions
chordDiagrams.description: Seventh chords add sophistication and are perfect for indie and alternative styles.
practiceNotes: These voicings work especially well for fingerpicking
Focus on letting notes ring together clearly

chordDiagrams.title: Key of G Major
chordDiagrams.description: A guitar-friendly key with easy open chord shapes - great for beginners.
practiceNotes: All open chords - great for beginners
Focus on smooth transitions between Em and C

advancedApplications.title: Upper Fret Voicings
advancedApplications.description: Barre chord voicings for smoother transitions and different tonal colors.
items: Am (5th fret): Barre chord voicing for smoother transitions
F (1st fret): Standard barre position
C (8th fret): Higher voicing with rich harmonics
G (3rd fret): Compact barre chord form

advancedApplications.title: Comparison with I-V-vi-IV
advancedApplications.description: Understanding how reordering the same chords changes the emotional arc.
items: I-V-vi-IV: Confident > Tension > Melancholy > Comfort
vi-IV-I-V: Melancholy > Comfort > Home > Anticipation
Starting on vi creates relative minor emphasis
The progression resolves optimistically rather than melancholically

advancedApplications.title: Common Keys Reference
advancedApplications.description: The vi-IV-I-V progression in the most commonly used keys for guitar.
items: Key of C: Am - F - C - G
Key of G: Em - C - G - D
Key of D: Bm - G - D - A
Key of A: F#m - D - A - E

practiceCategories.title: Progressive Practice Plan
items: Basic Changes: Master clean transitions between open chords
Rhythm Patterns: Start with simple down-strums, add complexity
Different Keys: Learn in G, D, and A major
Voice Leading: Practice alternate voicings for smoother changes
Song Application: Play along with famous songs using this progression
Creative Variations: Experiment with extensions and substitutions

practiceCategories.title: Practice Tips
items: Focus on the emotional character of each chord
Practice with a metronome to develop steady timing
Record yourself to hear the progression objectively
Try different tempos from ballad to uptempo
Experiment with dynamics (loud/soft) for emotional effect
Learn to loop the progression smoothly

practiceCategories.title: Emotional Mastery
items: Feel the shift from minor to major as you play
Use palm muting on the minor chord for contrast
Let the major chords ring out fully
Try arpeggiated patterns for a more intimate feel
Practice transitioning V back to vi for seamless looping

notatedExercises.title: Basic vi-IV-I-V (Key of C)
notatedExercises.description: Whole note chords in the key of C major. Focus on clean chord changes and even timing.
practiceNotes: Play each chord as a full strum, letting it ring for the entire measure
Focus on quick, clean transitions between chords
Use a metronome starting at 60 BPM

notatedExercises.title: Seventh Chord Variation
notatedExercises.description: The same progression using seventh chord extensions for a more sophisticated sound. Am7 - Fmaj7 - Cmaj7 - G7.
practiceNotes: Great for indie, alternative, and jazz-influenced styles
Notice how the seventh intervals add color to each chord
Focus on smooth voice leading between adjacent chords

notatedExercises.title: vi-IV-I-V in Key of G
notatedExercises.description: All open chords make this a great key for beginners to practice this progression. Em - C - G - D.
practiceNotes: All open chord shapes for easy transitions
Focus on the bass note movement: E - C - G - D
Try fingerpicking patterns to explore the sound

sections.title: Primary Scales
items: Major scale of the key (e.g., C major for Am-F-C-G)
Natural minor / Aeolian mode of the vi chord
Pentatonic major over the I and IV chords
Pentatonic minor over the vi chord

sections.title: Modal Options
items: Dorian mode over the vi chord for a brighter minor sound
Mixolydian mode over the V chord for bluesy flavor
Ionian mode for melodic playing over the I chord

sections.title: Harmonic Analysis
items: Same chords as I-V-vi-IV, reordered for emotional effect
Starting on vi creates relative minor emphasis
IV to I is a plagal ("Amen") cadence motion
V to vi (when looping) creates a deceptive cadence

sections.title: Voice Leading Principles
items: Common tones between adjacent chords create smooth motion
Bass movement: vi down to IV, up to I, up to V
Inner voices often move by step or stay on common tones
The V-vi transition at the loop point is the key emotional moment
